subject: lightning strike
title: What If You Were Struck by Lightning?

scenes.text: What if you were struck by lightning? About nine in ten people survive. The surprise is how.
Direct hits are rare: only about three to five percent of lightning injuries.
Most come from current spreading through the ground, or jumping sideways from something nearby that was hit.
In a fraction of a second, millions of volts pass through you. The biggest danger: your heart can stop instantly.
The pressure wave can burst your eardrums. Fern-shaped red marks may bloom on your skin, gone in days.
Survivors can face nerve damage for years. One American was struck seven times between 1942 and 1977, and survived every one.

description:
What if you were struck by lightning? Around 90% of people who are struck survive.
Direct strikes cause only about 3 to 5% of lightning injuries; side flashes and ground current cause most of the rest. Death usually comes from instant cardiac arrest. Survivors may have burst eardrums, burns, temporary fern-like Lichtenberg figures, and long-term nerve damage. Roy Sullivan was struck seven times between 1942 and 1977.

first_comment: About 40 million lightning strikes hit the ground in the US every year. Have you ever been closer to one than you liked?
